attributes.readMe: # Tree ## Summary The generic tree view: expand/collapse over any parent-child structure. The block owns the mechanics every tree re-derives — carets, indentation, per-node expansion that survives data refreshes (keyed by path, not object identity), descendant rollup counts — and yields each row's content to the consumer, because what a node LOOKS like is domain knowledge (an employee with an avatar, a task with a status pill). `buildTree` (the cycle-safe forest builder from `@cardstack/catalog/utils/build-tree`, re-exported here) turns a flat list plus a parent edge into the node shape; consumers with links-based nesting map their structure directly. ## Usage ```gts import { Tree, buildTree } from '@cardstack/catalog/components/tree'; <:row as |task meta|> {{task.cardTitle}} {{#if meta.hasChildren}}{{meta.descendantCount}} subtasks{{/if}} ``` Without a `row` block, CardDef items render as their atom. `TreeExample/campaign-tree` shows a campaign task with its four subtasks. An org chart is the other typical consumer: `buildTree(employees, (e) => e.manager?.id)`. ## Non-goals No drag-to-reparent — mutation is a command's job, and the first consumer that needs it names the interaction. No selection model beyond what the consumer's own row content wires. Not virtualized: a tree past a few hundred visible rows wants a different component, and pretending otherwise here would hide that cliff.
attributes.cardDescription: Expand and collapse over any parent-child structure, with per-node expansion that survives refreshes and descendant counts; the consumer renders each row.
